key_insight: Hybrid quantum-classical PINNs had 38–44% fewer parameters but took at least 10× longer than the classical PINN at every measured stage.
engineering_relevance: Benchmark wall-clock costs across forward passes and derivative computations rather than using parameter count as a proxy for computational efficiency.
method: Tested a classical PINN, four hybrid configurations, and size-matched classical controls on 1D seawater temperature diffusion.
Timed cumulative forward, first- and second-order input-gradient, and PDE-loss parameter-gradient stages with CPU-simulated quantum circuits.
Examined runtime scaling with qubit count, circuit depth, batch size, and simulator backend.
evidence_signal: Hybrids were 14–56× slower for forward passes and 10–97× slower for PDE-loss parameter gradients than the classical PINN, with approximately exponential runtime growth as qubit count increased over the tested range.
watch_item: These results concern a single diffusion benchmark with CPU-simulated circuits and do not establish runtime performance on quantum hardware.
paper_title: Fewer Parameters, Longer Runtimes: The Wall-Clock Cost of Hybrid Quantum Physics-Informed Neural Networks
